note: The reported symptom is the diagnostic itself (this is a diagnostic-quality/overload-resolution issue, not a crash), so the exit code cannot discriminate it from an ordinary diagnosed error -- both are E_FAIL. Clause 1 anchors the specific message quoted in the issue body verbatim. Clauses 2-3 require BOTH candidate notes -- `void f(unsigned int)` and `void f(int)` -- to appear after a `candidate function` note, so the predicate cannot be satisfied by an unrelated ambiguous-call error naming some other function `f` or a different overload set. This is a presence finding (the diagnostic fires when it should not, per the reporter and the maintainer), so no anti-vacuity clause is needed the way an absence predicate would require one -- a failed/rejected compile cannot manufacture this specific three-part match for free. Control: control-unsigned-literal.hlsl is the identical program with the call site changed to `f(1u)` (an explicitly-unsigned literal); the issue reports this compiles with no diagnostic at all, so it is run with --expect no-match to confirm the predicate does not fire on every use of `f`, only on the reported ambiguous case.
